resources.string: Connect your SFPanel server to manage containers, files and terminals in one place.
Use your SFPanel address, including the port. HTTPS is selected when you omit the scheme.
Tap a server to check its connection and open the panel.
Your first server starts here. Only its name and address are saved on this device.
Remove this saved address? The server and its data will remain available.
%1$s uses HTTP. Credentials and server data travel without encryption. Use this only on a trusted network, or configure HTTPS.
Enter an HTTP or HTTPS server address with an optional port. Paths, passwords and query strings are not supported.
Could not connect. Check the address, port, network and server status, then try again.
The certificate could not be verified. Use a trusted HTTPS certificate or install your server’s CA certificate in Android settings.
This address did not return a healthy SFPanel response. Check the address and server database status.
Server addresses stay on this device. Sign-in and two-factor authentication are handled by your server. The app adds no analytics.
Close the panel and clear cookies, site storage and cached pages for all servers on this device?
This closes the current panel. Finish any uploads or unsaved edits first.
The page could not be loaded.
This link leaves your SFPanel server:\n%1$s
No app is available to open this link.
Could not save this file. Check the connection and available storage.
Finish the current file download first.
Reconnect to your network and try again. Your saved server addresses are still available.
Write in your own language. Multiple lines are welcome.
Insert text into the active session. Enter is not added automatically. A shell without bracketed paste may execute embedded newlines.
Text inserted. Review it in the terminal before pressing Enter.
Open a connected terminal or AI session first.
No matching output in the active terminal.
